questions.prompt: Match each observability pillar to what it is best at.

pairs.right: Detailed record of what happened at a point
Cheap aggregated numbers for trends and alerts
Following one request's path across services

questions.explanation: Logs give detail, metrics give cheap aggregate trends for alerting, and traces show where a request spent time across services.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between monitoring and observability?

options.text: Monitoring watches for known problems; observability helps you understand new, unexpected behavior — the 'why'

questions.explanation: Monitoring checks for predefined, known conditions; observability lets you answer questions you didn't anticipate, explaining unexpected behavior.

questions.prompt: What does the RED method measure for a service?
questions.explanation: RED = Rate (requests/sec), Errors (failed requests), Duration (latency) — the key user-facing signals for a request-driven service.

questions.prompt: Why attach and propagate a trace id across services?

options.text: To correlate metrics, traces, and logs into one story for a single request

questions.explanation: A shared trace id lets you jump from a spiking metric to the slow trace to the explaining log lines — reconstructing one request's end-to-end story.

questions.prompt: Why should you alert on symptoms (SLOs) rather than every internal cause?

options.text: Cause-based alerts create alert fatigue and non-actionable pages; symptom/SLO alerts stay meaningful and user-focused

questions.explanation: Paging on every cause (like a CPU blip) buries on-call in noise. Alerting on user-facing symptoms tied to SLOs keeps pages urgent and actionable.

questions.prompt: What is a risk of using high-cardinality labels (like user id) on metrics?

options.text: Each label combination is a new time series, so storage and cost can explode

questions.explanation: Every distinct label combination creates a separate time series. High-cardinality labels like user id can generate millions of series, exploding storage and cost.
